title: Genesis 42. The Cup of Testing.
edition: AID Genesis, Layer 1 (the steward's manuscript); narration: Kristin voice (public domain)
level_note: text follows the narration phrase by phrase
verse_numbers: none in this text; none shown
phrases: Genesis 42. The Cup of Testing.
Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt.
Jacob said to his sons: Why do you look at one another?
I have heard that there is grain in Egypt.
Go down there, and buy for us from there,
so that we may live and not die.
Go down.
the same word.
Joseph went down to Egypt.
Now the brothers go down.
The ones who sent him down are now going down themselves.
The Cup that was sent to Egypt draws the ones who sent it.
The pit that received Joseph now receives his brothers,
not into the ground, but into the land where he was sold.
The descent that began with one brother now continues with ten.
Joseph's ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.
But Jacob did not send Benjamin, Joseph's brother, with his brothers,
for he said: Lest perhaps harm happen to him.
Benjamin stays.
The only remaining son of Rachel.
The brother who shared a mother with Joseph.
The father who lost one son of Rachel clutches the only piece of her he has left.
The Cup of favoritism, the same favoritism that made Joseph a target,
now holds Benjamin in its grip.
Jacob learned nothing from the coat of many colors.
He plays favorites again.
The father who was deceived is about to deceive himself again,
by holding too tight.
The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came,
for the famine was in the land of Canaan.
Joseph was the governor over the land.
It was he who sold to all the people of the land.
Joseph's brothers came and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.
The dream.
Chapter thirty-seven: the sheaves in the field,
the brothers' sheaves bowing to Joseph's.
Here it begins.
The Cup that went down through the pit, the prison, the forgetting,
the elevation, now the ones who stripped it are bowing to it.
The brothers who said: Will you indeed reign over us?
are bowing.
Face to the ground.
In Egypt.
Before the brother they sold.
Joseph saw his brothers.
He recognized them..he recognized them.
The same root that has run through three generations of deception,
in the mouths of Jacob, the brothers, Tamar.
Now Joseph recognizes them, but he does not announce it.
He remembers the dreams.
And he tests.
But they did not recognize him..
The recognition pattern inverts.
For three generations, recognition was used in deception, Jacob deceiving blind Isaac,
the brothers deceiving mourning Jacob, Tamar deceiving Judah.
Now the one who was wronged recognizes the ones who wronged him,
and they do not know.
The power of recognition has shifted from the deceiver to the wounded.
The Cup that was held by men who used seeing to deceive is now held by a man who uses seeing to test.
Joseph spoke roughly with them: Where did you come from?
They said: From the land of Canaan, to buy food.
He said: You are spies.
You have come to see the nakedness of the land.
They said: No, my lord.
Your servants have come to buy food.
We are all one man's sons.
We are honest men.
Your servants are not spies.
We are honest men.
The men who sold their brother, dipped his coat in blood,
and lied to their father for twenty years, say:
we are honest men.
The Cup of testing is held by a man who knows the truth.
The vessels that hold the lie are standing before him, claiming honesty.
He said: No,
but you have come to see the nakedness of the land.
They said: We, your servants, are twelve brothers,
the sons of one man in the land of Canaan.
And behold, the youngest is this day with our father.
And one is no more.
One is no more.
They say it to his face.
The brother they sold stands before them, robed in linen,
wearing a gold chain, bearing Pharaoh's ring, and they describe his absence.
Joseph hears them say he is gone.
And he knows he is standing right there.
The Cup that was thrown away is now the Cup they are asking for grain from.
And they do not know.
Joseph remembered the dreams which he had dreamed about them.
The dreams.
The sheaves.
The stars.
Twenty-two years have passed.
The boy who dreamed at seventeen is now thirty-nine.
The sheaves are bowing.
The dream that the brothers tried to kill,
We will see what will become of his dreams,
is being fulfilled by the brothers themselves.
They are the sheaves.
And they are bowing.
He put them all together into custody for three days.
Three days.
Again.
The cup-bearer and baker, three days.
The brothers, three days.
The three day pattern: the period between accusation and resolution.
Between the false and the true.
Between the dream and its interpretation.
On the third day, Joseph said to them: Do this, and live,
for I fear God.
I fear God.
The same Joseph who said interpretations belong to God and not I,
God,
now says I fear God to the men who don't know he is their brother.
The man who serves the Cup of integrity now holds the Cup of testing,
and his authority to test is grounded in the fear of the same God his brothers have forgotten.
If you are honest men,
let one of your brothers be bound in your prison.
But go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.
Bring your youngest brother to me.
So your words will be verified, and you will not die.
They did so.
Then they said to one another: We are guilty concerning our brother,
in that we saw the distress of his soul when he begged us,
and we would not listen.
Therefore this distress has come upon us.
The first confession.
Twenty years of silence.
The coat, the blood, the lie to their father.
Now, in an Egyptian prison,
standing before a man they don't know is their brother,
they confess to each other.
The conscience that was silent in chapter thirty-seven finally speaks.
We saw his distress.
He begged us.
We did not listen.
The Cup of testing has opened the Cup of guilt,
the one vessel the brothers have been carrying for two decades without opening.
Reuben answered: Didn't I tell you, saying:
Do not sin against the boy?
And you would not listen.
Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.
Reuben.
The fallen firstborn.
The one who tried to save Joseph and found an empty pit.
The one who lay with Bilhah.
The one who offered his own sons as a guarantee for Benjamin.
Still trying.
Still the voice of righteousness that no one listens to.
His blood is required.
The blood that was on the coat,
the goat's blood that was used to deceive Jacob,
is now spoken of as a debt.
The price of betrayal that has not been paid.
They did not know that Joseph understood them,
for there was an interpreter between them.
They did not know he understood.
The brothers speak in their own language.
The interpreter translates.
They think their confession is private.
But the brother they sold is hearing every word.
He turned from them and wept.
The only person in Genesis who weeps for the brothers' guilt.
Not for himself.
Not for the pit or the prison or the years.
For their guilt.
The Cup of testing is also the Cup of tears.
The brother who was wronged weeps for the ones who wronged him,
not in anger, not in vengeance, but in grief.
He hears them say: we are guilty.
And he weeps.
Then he returned to them and spoke to them.
And he took Simeon from among them and bound him before their eyes.
Simeon.
The second son.
The one who participated in the slaughter at Shechem alongside Levi.
The one who followed violence.
The brother kept back is not random.
Reuben tried to save Joseph, he is spared.
Simeon participated in the slaughter, he is bound.
The Cup of testing is precise.
Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain,
and to restore every man's money into his sack,
and to give them food for the way.
It was done for them.
The money.
The Cup of testing deepens.
The money that bought Joseph, twenty shekels of silver,
is now returned to the buyers' own sacks.
The price of betrayal comes back to them.
The silver they received for selling their brother is now placed in their grain sacks by the brother they sold.
The Cup that was sold for silver now returns silver to the sellers.
They loaded their donkeys with grain and departed.
As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place,
he saw his money, and behold,
it was in the mouth of his sack.
He said to his brothers: My money is restored!
And behold, it is in my sack!
Their hearts failed them, and they were afraid, saying to one another:
What is this that God has done to us?
What is this that God has done to us?
The brothers who said: we are guilty,
now see the money returned and fear.
The Cup of guilt produces the Cup of fear.
The silver that was the price of a brother now appears as a sign of divine judgment.
What has God done?
The brothers who forgot God for twenty years now see His hand in their sacks.
They came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan and told him all that had happened.
The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us.
He took us for spies.
We said: We are honest men.
We are twelve brothers, sons of our father.
One is no more.
The youngest is this day with our father in the land of Canaan.
The man said:
By this I will know that you are honest men.
Leave one brother with me.
Take grain for the famine of your houses and go.
Bring your youngest brother to me.
As they emptied their sacks, behold,
every man's bundle of money was in his sack.
When they and their father saw the bundles of money,
they were afraid.
Jacob their father said to them:
You have bereaved me of my children!
Joseph is no more.
Simeon is no more.
And you would take Benjamin.
All these things are against me.
All these things are against me.
The father who was deceived for twenty years still carries the wound.
He does not know Joseph is alive.
He does not know Simeon will be returned.
He does not know the money is a test, not a punishment.
He sees only loss.
Joseph, gone.
Simeon, gone.
Benjamin, threatened.
The Cup of the deceived father still holds the blood-stained coat.
The vessel that was lied to by his sons now believes every new event is another loss.
Reuben said to his father:
Kill my two sons if I do not bring him back to you.
Put him in my hands.
I will return him to you.
Jacob refused.
My son shall not go down with you.
For his brother is dead, and he alone is left.
If harm meets him on the way,
you will bring down my gray hairs in sorrow to Sheol.
The same refusal to let go.
Abraham could not let go of Isaac until God asked.
Jacob cannot let go of Benjamin.
The father who held the Cup of favoritism now holds the Cup of fear,
the fear that comes from having already lost one son and being asked to risk another.
The man who was told by God:
I am with you and will keep you wherever you go,
now says: all these things are against me.
The man who wrestled with God and was renamed Israel now speaks as Jacob,
the old name.
The deceiver who became the wrestler has become the father who is afraid.
The Cup of testing is held by three vessels.
Joseph, testing.
The brothers, guilty.
Jacob, afraid.
The brother who was sold is testing the brothers who sold him.
The brothers who sold him are feeling the guilt they buried.
The father who was lied to is reliving the loss.
Three cups.
One household.
The Cup of the covenant,
the promise that all nations would be blessed,
is now passing through a test that will determine whether this family can hold together or will shatter.
Benjamin must go.
The father must let go.
The brothers must face the one they wronged.
The Cup that was stolen must be returned, not as theft,
not as a bargain, but as trust.
The testing is not cruelty.
It is the necessary path from guilt to confession to reconciliation.
The Cup goes down before it rises.
The brothers went down to Egypt.
The testing went down into their conscience.
And the way back up,
the way to the brother they do not know is alive,
goes through Benjamin.
Through the one son Jacob will not release.
The Cup holds.
The test continues.
The dream is being fulfilled, sheaf by sheaf, brother by brother,
sack by sack.
And the brother who wept when he heard them confess is waiting.
